registry_info.name: isosurfaces
registry_info.description: Marching cubes, metaballs, implicit surfaces, and isosurface extraction artifacts

voxel_noise_demo.description: CPU marching cubes with 3D noise — the working cave/blob generator. Glass shader with wireframe overlay.
voxel_noise_demo.compute: HEAVY — CPU nested loop, generates mesh on ready
voxel_noise_demo.name: voxel_noise_demo
voxel_noise_demo.qfep_connection: The field before the surface: a lattice of samples, each holding one number — how inside am I here? Noise fills the grid with a landscape of values and no shape yet. The chapter's raw material, shown honestly as data.

gyroid_demo.description: GPU compute gyroid minimal surface — domain-warped, organic sculpture emerging from nothing. Triply periodic implicit function.
gyroid_demo.name: gyroid_demo
gyroid_demo.qfep_connection: A minimal surface no hand modeled: sin x cos y + sin y cos z + sin z cos x = 0. The gyroid divides all of space into two interpenetrating labyrinths that never touch — an equation wearing geometry.

fountain_demo.description: GPU compute fountain shape — vertical form generated by marching cubes.
fountain_demo.name: fountain_demo
fountain_demo.qfep_connection: The field animated: a surface re-extracted every frame as its function changes, geometry flowing like water because it *is* recomputation, not motion.

mc_sculpt_vr.description: GPU SDF sculpting — add spherical blobs with smooth union. Up to 500 blobs, real-time mesh extraction.
mc_sculpt_vr.qfep_connection: Sculpting by editing the field, not the mesh: your hand adds and subtracts density, and the surface follows as a consequence. Digital clay whose truth lives in the numbers underneath the visible skin.

mc_portal_landscape.description: GPU terrain with portal arches — landscape-scale marching cubes with embedded portal geometry.
mc_portal_landscape.name: mc_portal_landscape
mc_portal_landscape.qfep_connection: Two regimes of the same field joined by a portal — thresholds as doorways, the level-set constant as the architect of where you can pass.

mc_cave.description: GPU cave system — noise-driven marching cubes producing walkable cave geometry.
mc_cave.name: mc_cave
mc_cave.qfep_connection: The fifteen cases put to work at room scale — a cave marched out of a scalar field, the lookup table's alphabet suddenly speaking in caverns.

mc_torus_sculpture.description: GPU torus sculpture — marching cubes extracting torus isosurface.
mc_torus_sculpture.name: mc_torus_sculpture
mc_torus_sculpture.qfep_connection: A torus as a threshold event: the set of points where a field crosses zero. Walk around it and remember it has no polygons of its own — the mesh is the algorithm's testimony about the field.

mc_shapes_gallery.description: Gallery of multiple marching cubes shapes — sphere, torus, and more displayed side by side.
mc_shapes_gallery.name: mc_shapes_gallery
mc_shapes_gallery.qfep_connection: The extraction bestiary: spheres, tori, blends — each shape one implicit function passed through the same fifteen-case mill. The gallery's argument: the surface was never modeled, only *described*.

mc_inside_cave.description: GPU interior cave view — marching cubes cave seen from inside.
mc_inside_cave.name: mc_inside_cave
mc_inside_cave.qfep_connection: Standing inside the isosurface: the cave is where the field says *in*, and you are in it. The boundary wraps around the walker — geometry experienced from the wrong side of the skin.

mc_flat_landscape.description: GPU flat terrain — marching cubes landscape with gentle noise.
mc_flat_landscape.name: mc_flat_landscape
mc_flat_landscape.qfep_connection: A heightfield marched into terrain — the gentlest landscape the algorithm can speak, one value per column, the ground as a graph of a function.

mc_overhang_landscape.description: GPU overhang terrain — landscape with overhanging rock formations.
mc_overhang_landscape.name: mc_overhang_landscape
mc_overhang_landscape.qfep_connection: The terrain heightfields cannot make: overhangs. A full 3D field permits inside-above-outside, and the cliff leans over your head — the moment the third dimension of the data becomes visible as shelter.

animated_noise_explorer.description: Animated noise field explorer — watch marching cubes extract surfaces from evolving noise in real-time.
animated_noise_explorer.name: animated_noise_explorer
animated_noise_explorer.qfep_connection: Marching cubes run on a noise field that will not hold still — surfaces extracted from evolving randomness in real time, the skin re-found every frame as the field beneath it churns. The chapter's two neighbors married and set in motion: noise supplies the field, marching cubes reads the threshold, and the result is geometry that flows because its data does.

mc_base.description: Base GPU marching cubes scene — the core implementation.
mc_base.name: mc_base
mc_base.qfep_connection: The core marching-cubes scene on the GPU — the algorithm at its plainest, the base implementation everything else in the chapter is dressed from. The engine room: no landscape, no cave, just the fifteen cases running on the graphics card, the pure act of turning a field of numbers into a surface, shown without ornament.

nakama_metaballs.description: Kouhei Nakama-inspired organic metaballs — 60 animated blobs with subsurface scattering shader. Approximated mesh via sphere deformation.
nakama_metaballs.compute: HEAVY — CPU per-frame mesh rebuild with metaball field evaluation
nakama_metaballs.name: nakama_metaballs

raymarched_metaballs.description: Shader raymarched metaballs — 9 animated balls rendered via SDF raymarching on a cube mesh. Real-time implicit surface visualization.
raymarched_metaballs.compute: LIGHT — GPU shader only, no mesh extraction

metaball_world.description: Full marching cubes metaball system — proper isosurface extraction from metaball field. Animated, with collision. The real deal.
metaball_world.compute: HEAVY — CPU marching cubes, periodic mesh rebuild
metaball_world.name: metaball_world

fifteen_cases_demo.description: Interactive display of the 15 unique marching cubes cases (from 256 total). Educational — shows how the lookup table works.
fifteen_cases_demo.name: fifteen_cases_demo
fifteen_cases_demo.qfep_connection: The whole algorithm on one plinth: a cube has 8 corners, each in or out — 256 configurations that symmetry folds to 15. Every marching-cubes surface ever extracted is these fifteen tiles, looked up and glued. The lookup table as Rosetta stone.

rhizome_cave_demo.description: Rhizomatic cave — Deleuze-inspired branching cave generation using growth patterns + marching cubes.
rhizome_cave_demo.compute: HEAVY — CPU growth simulation + marching cubes
rhizome_cave_demo.name: rhizome_cave_demo
rhizome_cave_demo.qfep_connection: A cave grown as rhizome — Deleuze's centerless, multiply-connected figure carved into stone by branching growth and marching cubes. The post-crisis answer in geology: after the foundations fell, you build spaces with no single entrance and no privileged path, structures that are all middle. A world you enter anywhere and cross more than one way — formalization's limits turned into an architecture of the between.

mc_terrain_demo.description: CPU terrain generation demo — marching cubes terrain with configurable noise parameters.
mc_terrain_demo.name: mc_terrain_demo
mc_terrain_demo.qfep_connection: The terrain workbench: density thresholds, noise octaves, resolution — dials on a landscape. Turning them shows the ground to be an opinion held by a field.

queer_marching_cave.description: Extended cave system — long procedural cave with queer spatial topology themes.
queer_marching_cave.name: queer_marching_cave
queer_marching_cave.qfep_connection: The cave that refuses a single threshold: iso-values shifted, blended, contested. If inside/outside is just a number's relation to a cutoff, then the cutoff is a politics — this room marches the same field under a different regime and gets another world.

rhizome_cave_system.name: Rhizomatic Cave System
rhizome_cave_system.description: Advanced cave generation using rhizomatic growth patterns and marching cubes for organic underground networks

marching_squares.description: The isosurfaces seam. A smooth circle beside the same circle read on a coarse grid - a blocky disc (lego). The surface between the samples was never seen; detail finer than the spacing is gone.
marching_squares.name: Marching Squares
marching_squares.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for isosurfaces. Bias is conserved; show the seam.
